Here are a few arguments I can think of where you wouldn't want to buy an Xbox One to play in your living room along with an existing gaming PC:

  • cost - at $50 the Steam Link is going to be a much cheaper piece of hardware than a standalone console
  • ecosystem - if you're invested in Steam's ecosystem, it's easier to play the games you already own from your PC than it would be to buy and maintain a separate library of Xbox One games. Also you wouldn't have one-to-one compatibility with your existing library, since not all games are available on both platforms
  • subscription - you would need to maintain a separate Xbox Live subscription in order to play your living room games
  • friends list - you wouldn't be able to play with your PC friends on your living room machine because it's running on Xbox Live.

If you can mitigate these cons, the pros would be:

  • dedicated hardware - running the game on its own hardware grants better performance/reliability than streaming, although you could argue this with a dedicated living room PC as well
  • access to two ecosystems - cost aside, you would have access to exclusives on two platforms instead of one
  • friends list - you would be able to play with both PC and Xbox players, but it would require moving from machine to machine.

So while there are a number of pros and cons to each solution, the bottom line is that the Steam Link isn't really analogous to having a console in your living room since the experience is so different to each.
